intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Experience the cloud forest ecosystem from above while spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and sloths along the way. Most operators include a hanging bridges walk as part of the package.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Tortuguero Wildlife Canal Boat Tour
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero National Park on a guided boat tour. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, manatees, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night for an unforgettable wildlife encounter.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide. Discover nocturnal creatures including kinkajous, red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping birds, tarantulas, and stick insects. The cloud forest takes on an entirely different character at night, offering a rare and intimate wildlife experience unique to this biodiverse region.
experiences.location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, Puntarenas Province

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Guided Rainforest Hike & Beach Day
experiences.description: Hike through Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas hidden in the canopy. After the wildlife hike, relax on the park's pristine white-sand beaches — some of the most beautiful in Central America — with calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming.

experiences.name: Soda Viquez Traditional Costa Rican Cooking & Market Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Costa Rican food culture with a visit to a local mercado followed by a hands-on cooking experience at a family-run soda. Learn to prepare traditional dishes like gallo pinto, casado, and tres leches cake using fresh local ingredients. This cultural experience offers genuine insight into Tico daily life and culinary traditions passed down through generations.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport's affordable food court or a soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort if open late. Budget: $5–$10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance to save money vs. private taxi. Shared shuttles from SJO to the beach area typically cost $15–$25 USD per person. Keep snacks handy for the journey. Rest well — adventures begin tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a late breakfast, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get oriented. Explore the immediate surroundings of Aegean Bliss Resort and locate nearby amenities like supermarkets, ATMs, and local sodas (diners).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Spot local wildlife such as pelicans, howler monkeys in nearby trees, and colorful iguanas along the shoreline. This is a free activity perfect for budget travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town center for dinner. Explore the local nightlife scene with a cold Imperial beer (Costa Rica's iconic local lager) at a beachside bar. Watch the sunset over the Pacific Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Casado breakfast at the resort's nearest soda — rice, beans, egg, and fresh fruit juice. Budget: $4–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh fruit, bread, and snacks from a local supermarket (Super Mas or similar) for a DIY beach picnic. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local soda — try Gallo Pinto (rice and beans) with grilled chicken or fish. Budget: $6–$10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures (28–33°C / 82–91°F). Apply sunscreen generously. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at a local bank or ATM for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or mangrove estuary. Look for scarlet macaws, toucans, howler monkeys, white-faced capuchins, and coatis. Bring binoculars if available. Many coastal areas in Costa Rica have free or low-cost public trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge (such as Manuel Antonio, Carara, or Tortuguero depending on resort location). Entrance fees are typically $18–$20 USD for foreigners. Hire a local guide for a shared group tour to maximize wildlife spotting at a fraction of private tour costs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Cook a simple meal using groceries from a local supermarket or enjoy a budget-friendly dinner at a nearby soda. Share travel stories with fellow backpackers at the hostel common area or a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Pinto breakfast at a local soda with fresh papaya juice. Budget: $4–$6 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the supermarket — sandwiches, tropical fruit, and water. Budget: $5–$7 USD.
meals.dinner: Casado plate (rice, beans, salad, protein) at a local soda. Budget: $7–$10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at national parks early (opening is usually 7:00 AM) to beat crowds and catch the most wildlife activity. Wear neutral-colored clothing, closed-toe shoes, and bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING ADVENTURE DAY! Book a budget zip-line tour with a local operator in the nearest mountainous or forested area. Look for group discount rates or book through the resort's activity desk. Many operators offer packages from $45–$70 USD including transport, harness, and guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the zip-line experience with additional platforms and canopy walkways. After the tour, visit a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole for a refreshing dip — many are accessible for free or a small entrance fee of $2–$5 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your zip-lining adventure with dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant. Try traditional Costa Rican ceviche or fresh grilled fish (pargo or corvina) caught locally.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the tour — eggs, Gallo Pinto, toast, and coffee at a soda. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch is often included in zip-line tour packages. If not, grab a quick bite at a roadside soda near the tour operator. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at a beachfront restaurant. Look for the daily catch special. Budget: $10–$15 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-line tours at least 1–2 days in advance, especially in high season (February is peak season). Wear comfortable athletic clothing and closed-toe shoes. Leave valuables at the hotel. Weight restrictions typically apply (usually under 250 lbs / 113 kg).

day_by_day.morning: Eco-adventure kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) along the coastline or river estuary. Rental fees are typically $10–$20 USD per hour. Explore mangroves and spot crocodiles, herons, and kingfishers from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or reptile sanctuary. These eco-education centers typically charge $10–$15 USD entrance and offer guided tours explaining Costa Rica's incredible biodiversity and conservation efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk! Join a guided night tour ($20–$30 USD) to spot nocturnal creatures such as red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping birds, bats, and tarantulas. An unforgettable budget-friendly eco-adventure.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit smoothie bowl and toast at a local café. Budget: $5–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Arroz con Pollo (rice with chicken) at a roadside soda. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.dinner: Pre-night tour early dinner — try a burrito or empanadas from a local street food vendor. Budget: $4–$7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: For the night walk, wear long pants and closed-toe shoes to protect against insects and brush. Bring a flashlight or headlamp. Red-light mode on flashlights is preferred to avoid disturbing wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby volcano or hot springs area (e.g., Arenal Volcano region if accessible via shared shuttle). Budget shared shuttles run $20–$40 USD one way. Hike the volcano's lava trails with stunning views — entrance to Arenal Volcano National Park is approximately $18 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in natural hot springs near the volcano. Some public hot springs areas are free or very low cost ($5–$10 USD) compared to resort hot springs. Enjoy the therapeutic volcanic waters surrounded by lush rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return via shared shuttle. If staying overnight near Arenal, find budget accommodation at a local hostel ($15–$25 USD/night). Enjoy dinner in La Fortuna town center.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the supermarket for the early shuttle ride — bananas, granola bars, and water. Budget: $3–$5 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch in La Fortuna at a local soda — casado with fresh lemonade. Budget: $6–$9 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna — try Soda Viquez or similar local spots for authentic Tico food. Budget: $7–$11 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This may require an overnight stay depending on your resort's location. February offers clear views of Arenal Volcano with minimal cloud cover. Book shared shuttles in advance through Interbus or Grayline for budget rates.

day_by_day.morning: If near Arenal: Morning hanging bridges walk through the rainforest canopy. The Arenal Hanging Bridges park charges approximately $24 USD and offers stunning views of the volcano and diverse wildlife including sloths, toucans, and poison dart frogs.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Toro River (Class II–III rapids, great for beginners). Budget operators offer trips from $35–$55 USD including equipment and guides. An exhilarating eco-adventure through pristine jungle corridors.
day_by_day.evening: Return shuttle to the coast or continue exploring the Arenal area. Enjoy a well-deserved rest and a hearty dinner to refuel after an action-packed day.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or hotel breakfast — eggs, Gallo Pinto, and coffee. Budget: $4–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch often included with rafting tour. If not, grab food at a riverside soda. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or fish with patacones (fried plantains) at a local restaurant. Budget: $8–$12 USD.

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting operators provide all safety equipment. Wear a swimsuit under quick-dry clothes. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and camera. Tip your guides if service was excellent — $5–$10 USD is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort if you were on a multi-day excursion. Alternatively, visit a local wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary near the resort. Many centers accept volunteers or visitors for $10–$20 USD, allowing close encounters with rescued sloths, monkeys, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion off the coast. Rent snorkel gear ($10–$15 USD) or join a budget group boat tour ($25–$40 USD) to explore coral reefs and spot tropical fish, sea turtles, rays, and colorful marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside bonfire (if permitted) or join other travelers at a local beach bar. Try a Guaro Sour (Costa Rica's national spirit cocktail) or a fresh coconut water straight from the shell.

meals.breakfast: Pinto with fried egg and natilla (sour cream) at a beachside soda. Budget: $4–$6 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche and patacones from a beachfront kiosk. Budget: $6–$9 USD.
meals.dinner: BBQ fish tacos at a local beach restaurant. Budget: $8–$12 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling is best in the morning when water visibility is highest. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only to protect coral ecosystems. Costa Rica has strict environmental regulations — respect all marine life and never touch coral.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding through the jungle or along the beach. Local operators offer 2–3 hour rides for $30–$50 USD. A fantastic way to explore the landscape while spotting wildlife from a different vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or coffee/chocolate plantation tour. Costa Rica is world-famous for its coffee and cacao. Tours typically cost $15–$25 USD and include tastings. Learn about sustainable farming practices central to Costa Rica's eco-tourism model.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at a local home or community kitchen. Learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like Olla de Carne (beef stew), Tres Leches cake, or fresh tortillas. Budget cooking classes run $20–$35 USD and include dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate with granola and yogurt at a local café. Budget: $5–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the farm/plantation tour — often included or available for purchase. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner is included in the cooking class experience. Budget: $20–$35 USD (class fee).

day_by_day.notes: Book horseback riding and cooking classes through your hotel activity desk or local tour operators to get the best rates. Always verify operator credentials for animal welfare standards before booking horseback tours.

day_by_day.morning: Hiking day! Research nearby free or low-cost hiking trails. Many coastal areas have trails leading to secluded beaches, viewpoints, or waterfalls. Bring plenty of water (2L minimum), sunscreen, and a trail map downloaded offline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach a hidden waterfall or secluded beach accessible only by trail. Swim in the natural pool, relax, and enjoy the pristine surroundings. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy in this remote paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga on the beach (many resorts and local instructors offer free or donation-based beach yoga sessions). Reflect on your eco-adventures over a peaceful beachside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Energizing breakfast before the hike — oatmeal, banana, and coffee from a local soda. Budget: $4–$6 USD.
meals.lunch: DIY picnic packed from the supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and electrolyte drinks. Budget: $6–$9 USD.
meals.dinner: Grilled whole fish (pargo) with rice and salad at a beachfront restaurant. Budget: $10–$14 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Always tell someone your hiking plan and expected return time. Stay on marked trails to protect wildlife habitats and avoid getting lost. Carry a first aid kit with blister plasters, antiseptic, and insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Sea turtle watching excursion (February is nesting/hatching season on some Costa Rican beaches). Join a certified eco-tour operator for a responsible wildlife watching experience ($25–$45 USD). These tours are strictly regulated to protect the turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby indigenous community or cultural center to learn about Costa Rica's pre-Columbian heritage. Many communities offer affordable guided tours, craft demonstrations, and traditional food tastings for $10–$20 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner with fellow travelers you've met during the trip. Choose a slightly elevated local restaurant to celebrate your Costa Rican adventure. Try Chifrijo (a beloved Costa Rican bar snack of rice, beans, pork, and pico de gallo).

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before the turtle tour (tours often depart at 5:00–6:00 AM). Granola bars and coffee to go. Budget: $3–$5 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the indigenous community cultural center or a nearby soda. Budget: $6–$9 USD.
meals.dinner: Celebratory group dinner at a local restaurant with Chifrijo and Imperial beers. Budget: $12–$18 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle tours must be booked with certified operators who follow strict SINAC (Costa Rica's national conservation system) guidelines. No flash photography, no touching turtles, and follow all guide instructions. This is a bucket-list wildlife experience.

day_by_day.morning: Last full day — revisit your favorite spot from the trip for a nostalgic morning. Whether it's the beach, a trail, or a wildlife area, spend quality time soaking in Costa Rica's incredible natural beauty one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping at local markets. Look for handmade crafts, Boruca masks, locally produced coffee, artisan chocolate, and natural products. Bargain respectfully and buy directly from artisans when possible to support local communities. Budget: $20–$50 USD for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset beach walk. Reflect on 13 incredible days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and cultural experiences. Enjoy a final dinner at your favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Tico breakfast — Gallo Pinto, eggs, cheese, plantains, and coffee. Budget: $5–$8 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café — fresh fruit smoothie and a sandwich. Budget: $6–$9 USD.
meals.dinner: Final dinner — splurge slightly on a special meal. Try Sopa Negra (black bean soup) to start and grilled lobster or fresh catch as the main course. Budget: $15–$25 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and prepare for departure tomorrow. Keep travel documents, boarding passes, and passport easily accessible. Set multiple alarms for your departure day. Exchange remaining Colones back to USD at the airport (keep some as souvenirs!).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wake-up for departure preparations. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — confirm checkout time with reception the night before to avoid extra charges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) via pre-booked shared shuttle. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Complete check-in, security, and immigration procedures. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Costa Rican coffee or chocolate gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Reflect on 13 unforgettable days in one of the world's premier eco-tourism destinations. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Costa Rican breakfast at a local soda near the resort. Budget: $4–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Airport food court meal or pack snacks from the supermarket for the flight. Budget: $8–$15 USD.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days: Accommodation (if additional nights needed): $15–$30/night at hostels. Activities total: $150–$250 USD. Food total: $130–$200 USD. Transport total: $80–$120 USD. Souvenirs: $20–$50 USD. Approximate total trip budget: $400–$650 USD excluding flights. Pura Vida — may the spirit of Costa Rica travel home with you!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked private shuttle or official taxi to your hotel. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Quick orientation of the property.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a 24-hour soda (local diner) near the resort if available. Budget ~$10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid unreliable taxis at night. Have local colones or USD ready for tips. Confirm all upcoming tour bookings before sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort restaurant. Take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and acclimate to the tropical environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort on foot or by bicycle rental. Visit a nearby town market or souvenir strip. Stop at a local soda for a fresh fruit smoothie and casado plate. Begin planning your week with the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk on the beach followed by dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range seafood restaurant. Enjoy a welcome cocktail (guaro sour or Imperial beer) and decompress.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – included or ~$12–18. Try gallo pinto (rice and beans), fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Local soda near the resort – casado with fish or chicken, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront restaurant – grilled catch of the day with patacones and salad, ~$18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a rest and orientation day. Stay hydrated – the tropical heat and humidity can be intense after a long flight. Apply sunscreen early. Pick up a local SIM card if you haven't already for maps and communication.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by shuttle or rental car toward Tortuguero National Park. The journey involves a combination of road and boat travel (approx. 3–4 hours total). Enjoy the scenic boat ride through jungle canals on arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero Wildlife Canal Boat Tour – Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero National Park on a guided boat tour. Spot caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, poison dart frogs, and a spectacular variety of tropical birds. Your naturalist guide will provide expert commentary throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small village of Tortuguero on foot. Browse local artisan shops and enjoy dinner at a lodge-side restaurant. If staying overnight in Tortuguero, check in to a mid-range jungle lodge. Evening walk along the beach (sea turtle nesting season varies – ask your guide).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – gallo pinto and eggs, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by tour operator on the boat, or stop at a local Tortuguero village soda – rice, beans, and fresh fish, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Tortuguero lodge restaurant – Caribbean-style rice and beans with chicken or shrimp in coconut milk, ~$15–22.

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small plane – no roads. Wear light, quick-dry clothing and bring rain gear, insect repellent, and waterproof bags for electronics. Book the canal tour in advance. This is a full travel-and-activity day so pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the Tortuguero canals with a local guide before the heat peaks. Look for Jesus Christ lizards, toucans, and green iguanas. Return to lodge for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero by boat and shuttle, heading toward the Arenal Volcano region (approx. 4–5 hours). Check in to a mid-range lodge or hotel in La Fortuna with views of Arenal Volcano.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Arenal hot springs (Tabacón, Baldi, or EcoTermales – mid-range entry ~$40–60 per person). These geothermally heated pools surrounded by jungle are a perfect recovery after travel days. Dinner at the hot springs restaurant or a local La Fortuna eatery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tortuguero lodge before departure – tropical fruit, eggs, and coffee, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Roadside soda during transit – casado or arroz con pollo, ~$8–10.
meals.dinner: Restaurant at or near the hot springs – Costa Rican fusion cuisine, ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Tortuguero to Arenal passes through beautiful northern lowlands. Consider stopping at a roadside fruit stand for fresh pineapple or watermelon. Book hot springs in advance as they fill up quickly in high season (February is peak season).

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour – Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano and Lake Arenal. Most tours include Tarzan swings, hanging bridges, and rappelling. Departs around 8:00 AM and lasts approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges (Puentes Colgantes) for a peaceful walk through primary rainforest at canopy level. Spot sloths, toucans, and howler monkeys at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna town for dinner. Browse the central park area. Optional: attend a local cultural event or live music at a bar near the main strip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your lodge before the zip-line tour – gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh juice, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hanging bridges café or a nearby soda – sandwich, fruit, and lemonade, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: La Fortuna town restaurant – try a wood-fired pizza or local steak house for a mid-range treat, ~$15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for zip-lining. Leave valuables at the hotel. Most canopy operators provide helmets and harnesses. The hanging bridges are best in the morning when wildlife is most active – afternoon visit is still worthwhile. Bring binoculars.

day_by_day.morning: Guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal with views of the volcano. A peaceful and scenic way to experience the region from a different angle. Tours depart around 7:30–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the La Fortuna Waterfall (Catarata La Fortuna). Hike down approximately 500 steps to reach this spectacular 70-meter waterfall and swim in the natural pool at its base. Allow 2–3 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart La Fortuna by shuttle toward Monteverde (approx. 3–4 hours via jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal – a scenic and iconic Costa Rican journey). Check in to a mid-range Monteverde lodge.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before kayaking – smoothie bowl or eggs with gallo pinto, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch by the waterfall or at a nearby soda – empanadas and fresh fruit, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Monteverde town restaurant upon arrival – vegetarian-friendly options abound here, try a local casado or pasta, ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal is one of Costa Rica's most memorable transport experiences and avoids a long road detour. Book in advance through your hotel or a reputable operator. The roads to Monteverde are notoriously bumpy – prepare for a rugged ride in the final stretch.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk – Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide. Discover nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tarantulas, glass frogs, sleeping birds, and the elusive olingo. Tours typically run 6:00–8:30 PM, but morning is free for rest or exploration. Morning: visit the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve for a self-guided or guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Frog Pond – two excellent mid-range attractions that showcase the incredible biodiversity of the region. Learn about the life cycles of hundreds of exotic butterfly and frog species.
day_by_day.evening: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk (6:00–8:30 PM). After the walk, enjoy a warm dinner at a cozy Monteverde restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – cloud forest lodges often serve excellent homemade breakfasts with local coffee, ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Café in Monteverde town – try a palmito (heart of palm) salad or a chorreado (corn pancake) with natilla, ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: Monteverde restaurant post-night walk – hearty soup or pasta to warm up after the cool cloud forest evening, ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde sits at approximately 1,500 meters elevation – bring a light jacket or fleece as evenings can be cool and misty. The night walk requires comfortable closed-toe shoes. Cameras with good low-light capability are recommended. Book the night walk in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Guided birdwatching tour in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve. February is excellent for spotting the resplendent quetzal – one of the most spectacular birds in the Americas. Depart at 6:00 AM with a certified birding guide for the best sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (CACTU) for a guided tour and tasting – a beloved local institution producing artisanal cheeses since the 1950s. Afterward, browse the Monteverde artisan market for handmade crafts and local coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Monteverde by shuttle toward Manuel Antonio on the Pacific coast (approx. 4–5 hours). Arrive and check in to your beachfront accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort or nearby mid-range hotel.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast before birdwatching – granola, banana, and coffee, ~$8–10.
meals.lunch: Cheese factory café – sample local cheeses, bread, and fresh juice, ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Manuel Antonio restaurant upon arrival – fresh Pacific seafood, ceviche, or grilled fish, ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The quetzal is most active in early morning – the 6:00 AM start is essential. Bring binoculars and a telephoto lens if possible. The drive to Manuel Antonio is long but scenic. Consider a mid-journey stop in Quepos for a quick stretch and snack.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio Guided Rainforest Hike & Beach Day – Hike through Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal camouflaged wildlife. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, iguanas, and over 100 bird species along the primary forest trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine white-sand beaches within Manuel Antonio National Park. Swim, snorkel, or simply enjoy the stunning scenery. The park closes at 4:00 PM – plan accordingly.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a Manuel Antonio clifftop bar with panoramic ocean views. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the Manuel Antonio strip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort or nearby café before entering the park – gallo pinto and eggs, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the beach (bring your own from a nearby soda or market) – sandwiches, fruit, and water, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Manuel Antonio restaurant – try whole fried red snapper (pargo) with patacones and salad, ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park is one of the most visited parks in Costa Rica – arrive early (park opens at 7:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. Book your naturalist guide in advance. Do not feed wildlife. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes, and plenty of water. Monkeys are notorious for stealing unattended bags.

day_by_day.morning: Soda Viquez Traditional Costa Rican Cooking & Market Tour – Immerse yourself in authentic Costa Rican food culture with a visit to a local mercado followed by a hands-on cooking class. Learn to prepare traditional dishes like gallo pinto, olla de carne, and tres leches cake using fresh local ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon at leisure. Options include: kayaking or paddleboarding in the calm waters near Manuel Antonio, visiting a local surf school for a beginner lesson, or exploring the Quepos town market for fresh tropical fruits and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner at one of Manuel Antonio's finest mid-range restaurants. Enjoy a multi-course meal with fresh Pacific seafood and a glass of local guaro or imported wine.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cooking tour – fresh fruit and coffee at the resort, ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared during the cooking class – included in the tour experience.
meals.dinner: Upscale mid-range Manuel Antonio restaurant – tasting menu or à la carte with ocean views, ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking tour is a fantastic cultural experience and a great way to bring Costa Rican recipes home. Ask the instructor for a recipe card to recreate dishes at home. Book in advance as class sizes are limited. The afternoon is intentionally free to allow flexibility and relaxation.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the Tarcoles River (approximately 1.5 hours from Manuel Antonio). This river is famous for having one of the highest concentrations of American crocodiles in the world. Walk the bridge for free crocodile spotting or join a guided boat tour for closer encounters and birding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Jacó or return to Manuel Antonio. If in Jacó: explore the surf town, rent a bike along the beach boulevard, or take a surf lesson. If back at Manuel Antonio: enjoy a final afternoon at the resort pool or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort – spa treatment (if available), sunset from the beach, or a quiet dinner at the resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure – gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee, ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or Jacó restaurant – fish tacos or a fresh ceviche, ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – enjoy a relaxed dinner with ocean views, ~$18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tarcoles River bridge crocodile viewing is free and one of Costa Rica's most unique experiences. Best viewed in the morning when crocodiles are most active. If doing a boat tour, book through a reputable operator. The drive from Manuel Antonio to Tarcoles is approximately 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: choose from a morning horseback riding tour through coastal rainforest and along the beach, a whale and dolphin watching boat tour (February is excellent for humpback whales in the Southern Pacific), or a relaxed yoga class on the beach at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping in Quepos or Manuel Antonio – pick up local coffee, chocolate, artisan jewelry, and hand-painted crafts. Visit a local coffee plantation tour if time permits for a behind-the-scenes look at Costa Rica's famous coffee production.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final dinner at the best mid-range restaurant in Manuel Antonio. Reflect on the journey over a feast of fresh seafood, tropical cocktails, and dessert. Pack bags for early departure the following day.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – full spread with tropical fruits, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee, ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Quepos market or local soda – try a chiverre empanada or tamale, ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Top-rated mid-range Manuel Antonio restaurant – grilled lobster or whole fish with Caribbean rice, plantains, and a local craft beer, ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in February is excellent along the Pacific coast – book through a certified eco-operator that follows responsible whale watching guidelines. Pack bags tonight and set an alarm for an early start tomorrow. Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach or a last dip in the ocean. Enjoy a leisurely checkout breakfast at the resort. Settle any outstanding bills and tip hotel staff appropriately (tipping is customary in Costa Rica).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) in San José – approximately 3–3.5 hours from Manuel Antonio. Allow extra time for traffic, especially on weekends. Alternatively, if flying from Quepos (La Managua Airport), it is only 10 minutes away and serves domestic connections to SJO.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Browse duty-free for last-minute Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, or Lizano sauce. Reflect on an incredible 13-day adventure through volcanoes, cloud forests, jungles, canals, and Pacific beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – go all out with a full gallo pinto spread and fresh Costa Rican coffee, ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café – light meal before the flight, ~$12–20.
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in, security, and immigration at SJO. The airport has good dining and shopping options. Consider purchasing vacuum-sealed Costa Rican coffee (Café Britt or Volcanica) at the airport as gifts – it is allowed through customs. Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Experience the cloud forest ecosystem from above while spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and sloths along the way. Most operators include a hanging bridges walk as part of the package.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Tortuguero Wildlife Canal Boat Tour
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero National Park on a guided boat tour. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, manatees, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night for an unforgettable wildlife encounter.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide. Discover nocturnal creatures including kinkajous, red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping birds, tarantulas, and stick insects. The cloud forest takes on an entirely different character at night, offering a rare and intimate wildlife experience unique to this biodiverse region.
experiences.location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, Puntarenas Province

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Guided Rainforest Hike & Beach Day
experiences.description: Hike through Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas hidden in the canopy. After the wildlife hike, relax on the park's pristine white-sand beaches — some of the most beautiful in Central America — with calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming.

experiences.name: Soda Viquez Traditional Costa Rican Cooking & Market Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Costa Rican food culture with a visit to a local mercado followed by a hands-on cooking experience at a family-run soda. Learn to prepare traditional dishes like gallo pinto, casado, and tres leches cake using fresh local ingredients. This cultural experience offers genuine insight into Tico daily life and culinary traditions passed down through generations.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome amenity and late-night snack prepared by the resort upon check-in.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort — artisan cheeses, tropical fruits, and a glass of premium Costa Rican craft beer or sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged and confirmed. Resort concierge will be on standby for late arrival. Luggage handling and express check-in included with luxury package. Rest well — adventures begin tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast with ocean views. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront property, meet your dedicated concierge, and review the full 13-day itinerary over fresh-pressed tropical juice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort beach experience — snorkeling in the crystal-clear Pacific waters, paddleboarding, or simply relaxing in a shaded cabana with personalized butler service. Optional guided tide pool exploration with a resort naturalist.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's infinity bar overlooking the Pacific. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict with local chorizo, fresh-baked pastries, and specialty Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort's beach club — ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced Costa Rican ingredients, paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day after late arrival. Use this time to acclimate, hydrate, and confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the concierge. Apply sunscreen generously — the Costa Rican sun is intense even in February.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle for Tortuguero National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours). En route, stop at a premium eco-lodge for a mid-morning refreshment break surrounded by rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero Wildlife Canal Boat Tour — glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero National Park on a private guided boat tour. Spot caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, and a spectacular array of tropical birds including toucans and herons. Your expert naturalist guide will provide in-depth commentary throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort via private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — grab-and-go premium box also available for the road
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served aboard or alongside the canal boat — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruits, local snacks, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's secondary restaurant featuring Caribbean-inspired Costa Rican cuisine — rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, fresh grilled snapper, and plantain desserts

day_by_day.notes: Wear lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing and waterproof footwear. Bring insect repellent, binoculars, and a camera with zoom capability. The private boat tour ensures maximum wildlife viewing with minimal crowds. February is an excellent dry season month for wildlife spotting in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio Guided Rainforest Hike — hike through Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Observe white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and rare amphibians hidden in the dense foliage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition from jungle to paradise — spend the afternoon on Manuel Antonio's world-famous white-sand beach. Swim in calm turquoise waters, relax under a private shaded setup arranged by your guide, or explore the rocky headlands for more wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top-rated restaurant in the Manuel Antonio area before returning to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch at La Luna Restaurant at Gaia Hotel & Reserve — one of the finest dining experiences in the Manuel Antonio area, with panoramic jungle and ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kapi Kapi Restaurant, Manuel Antonio — renowned for its fusion of Asian and Costa Rican flavors using fresh local ingredients; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers — ensure entry tickets are pre-booked. The park opens at 7:00 AM; an early start maximizes wildlife sightings before midday heat. Bring water shoes for the beach and a dry bag for valuables. Monkeys are bold — keep food secured.

day_by_day.morning: Private resort yoga session on the beach at sunrise led by a certified instructor. Follow with a therapeutic spa treatment at the Aegean Bliss Resort spa — choose from a deep tissue massage, volcanic mud wrap, or a signature Costa Rican coffee body scrub.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soda Viquez Traditional Costa Rican Cooking & Market Tour — immerse yourself in authentic Costa Rican food culture with a visit to a vibrant local mercado. Shop for exotic spices, tropical fruits, and artisan products, then participate in a hands-on cooking class preparing traditional dishes like gallo pinto, casado, and tres leches cake.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you prepared during the cooking class as part of a communal dinner experience with your hosts. Return to the resort for a nightcap at the infinity bar.

meals.breakfast: Light post-yoga breakfast at the resort — açaí bowls, fresh fruit, granola, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Tastings and snacks at the local mercado during the market tour — sample fresh tropical fruits, local cheeses, and street-style Costa Rican bites
meals.dinner: Traditional Costa Rican feast prepared during the Soda Viquez cooking class — gallo pinto, slow-cooked beef, fried plantains, and homemade tortillas

day_by_day.notes: The cooking and market tour is an excellent cultural counterbalance to the nature-heavy days. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market. Bring a reusable bag for any artisan purchases. The spa should be booked at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer departs early for the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours from the beachfront resort). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's lush interior highlands. Arrive and check into a premium eco-lodge near Arenal for a two-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in and enjoy the eco-lodge's amenities — many feature natural hot springs fed by Arenal's geothermal activity. Soak in thermal pools with views of the volcano, enjoy light spa treatments, or take a short guided nature walk on the lodge grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Arenal Volcano (weather permitting — February is generally clear) from the lodge terrace. Dinner at the lodge's fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Stop en route at a recommended roadside restaurant in La Fortuna — try the local specialty of fresh trout from the highlands
meals.dinner: Dinner at the eco-lodge restaurant near Arenal — farm-to-table menu featuring locally grown vegetables, free-range meats, and artisan cheeses from the region

day_by_day.notes: Recommended premium eco-lodges near Arenal include Nayara Springs or Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort — confirm your lodge booking well in advance as these fill quickly. Pack a light jacket as evenings near Arenal can be cooler than the coast. The volcano is most visible in the morning before clouds build.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano and Lake Arenal. The premium tour includes a private guide, top-of-the-line safety equipment, and a small exclusive group for maximum enjoyment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-adrenaline recovery at the natural hot springs — enjoy the therapeutic geothermal pools at your eco-lodge or upgrade to a premium day pass at Tabacón Hot Springs, the most celebrated thermal resort in Costa Rica. Indulge in a riverside massage.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night walk near Arenal — discover nocturnal rainforest wildlife including red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, and exotic insects with a local naturalist guide. Return to the lodge for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full eco-lodge breakfast — eggs prepared to order, fresh tropical fruits, local bread, and Costa Rican specialty coffee from the Arenal region
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a restaurant overlooking Lake Arenal — grilled meats, fresh salads, and cold local craft beer
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner at the eco-lodge — candlelit terrace dining with volcano views, featuring a special tasting menu with paired Costa Rican craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour departs early morning — wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. The combination of zip-lining in the morning and hot springs in the afternoon is the quintessential Arenal experience. The night walk should be booked through the lodge concierge and typically lasts 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk around Lake Arenal with a specialist ornithologist guide — February is prime dry season and excellent for spotting toucans, kingfishers, and the resplendent quetzal in higher elevations. Optional kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer departs for Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 2.5–3 hours on scenic mountain roads). Arrive and check into a premium cloud forest lodge. Take a gentle introductory walk on the lodge's private reserve trails.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Monteverde. Enjoy cocktails at the lodge bar while watching the cloud forest mist roll in at dusk — a truly magical experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal eco-lodge before departure — hearty options to fuel the morning activities
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Santa Elena, Monteverde's charming village — dine at a recommended farm-to-table café
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Monteverde lodge restaurant — cloud forest cuisine featuring local dairy products, organic vegetables, and highland trout

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde is famously winding and unpaved in sections — a 4WD vehicle is standard for private transfers. Travel time can vary. Monteverde is cooler and mistier than the coast — pack a light rain jacket and layers. Recommended premium lodges include Belmar Hotel or El Silencio Lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — private guided tour through one of the world's most biodiverse ecosystems. Walk suspended bridges over the forest canopy, search for the elusive resplendent quetzal, and marvel at orchids, bromeliads, and moss-draped trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — observe dozens of exotic butterfly species and watch hundreds of hummingbirds feed at close range. Optional visit to a premium artisan cheese factory for a tasting of Monteverde's famous dairy products.
day_by_day.evening: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk — explore the mystical cloud forest after dark with an expert naturalist guide. Discover nocturnal creatures including sleeping birds, tarantulas, glass frogs, and the rare olingo. Return for a warming nightcap at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — warm porridge, fresh-baked bread, local cheeses, and hot chocolate made from Costa Rican cacao
meals.lunch: Lunch at Celajes Restaurant at Belmar Hotel — panoramic cloud forest views with a sophisticated farm-to-table menu
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — slow-cooked highland dishes, artisan cheese boards, and a glass of premium Costa Rican rum

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve is best visited early morning when wildlife is most active and crowds are minimal. Wear waterproof layers and sturdy hiking boots — the cloud forest is perpetually damp. The night walk is one of the most memorable experiences in Costa Rica and should not be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Coffee plantation tour in the Monteverde highlands — visit a premium organic coffee farm for a behind-the-scenes look at Costa Rica's world-famous coffee production, from bean to cup. Participate in a cupping session and purchase freshly roasted beans to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic descent from the cloud forest to the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome-back cocktail at the infinity bar and a relaxed dinner to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Final cloud forest breakfast at the Monteverde lodge — fuel up for the travel day
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box for the road — prepared by the lodge with gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — light seafood dishes, fresh salads, and a dessert of local tropical fruits with cream

day_by_day.notes: The return journey to the coast is long but scenic. Coordinate with your private driver for comfort stops. Upon return to the resort, confirm the final days' activities with the concierge and arrange any last spa treatments or excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Private sport fishing charter — depart at dawn from the nearest marina for a world-class offshore fishing experience in the Pacific. Costa Rica's waters are legendary for sailfish, marlin, mahi-mahi, and yellowfin tuna. Your luxury charter includes a captain, first mate, and all premium equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the marina by early afternoon. If catch-and-release is not preferred, arrange for your catch to be prepared by the resort's chef for a private dinner. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at the resort pool or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef dinner on the beach — a bespoke dining experience set up on the sand with torchlight, a dedicated server, and a custom menu prepared by the resort's head chef using your fresh catch or premium local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before the fishing charter — fresh fruit, yogurt, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch aboard the fishing charter — fresh ceviche, sandwiches, cold drinks, and tropical snacks
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beach dinner — grilled fresh catch of the day, lobster, or premium cuts with fine wine pairings under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Sport fishing charters should be pre-booked through the resort concierge. February is excellent for offshore fishing in Costa Rica. The private beach dinner must be arranged at least 48 hours in advance — this is a highlight experience and worth the planning effort. Bring sunscreen and polarized sunglasses for the fishing charter.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury spa morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — begin with a sunrise meditation session on the beach, followed by a 90-minute signature treatment (volcanic stone massage, rainforest body wrap, or hydrotherapy circuit). This is a dedicated wellness and relaxation day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to a nearby marine reserve — explore vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, rays, and reef sharks. A certified dive master accompanies the group for safety and guidance. Non-divers can enjoy glass-bottom boat viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail hour at the resort's infinity pool bar — reflect on the journey with fellow travelers or in peaceful solitude. Final gourmet dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Spa-appropriate light breakfast — green smoothies, overnight oats, fresh berries, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled seafood, fresh salads, and chilled tropical juices
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — chef's special tasting menu with premium wine pairings, celebrating 13 days of extraordinary Costa Rican adventure

day_by_day.notes: This penultimate day is intentionally designed as a luxurious wind-down before departure. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer logistics with the concierge. Begin packing and organizing any souvenirs, coffee, and artisan goods purchased throughout the trip. The marine excursion requires a moderate swim ability.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — take in the last moments of Costa Rica's stunning Pacific coastline. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort with time to savor every detail. Visit the gift shop for any final artisan souvenirs, locally roasted coffee, or Costa Rican chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort checkout and private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport in San José. The drive is approximately 3–4 hours depending on traffic — depart with ample time for international flight check-in. En route, make a brief stop at a premium souvenir market if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, zip-lining through cloud forests, and world-class luxury hospitality. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the resort — a full gourmet spread to savor before departure
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a farewell lunch stop en route — the resort concierge can recommend a premium restaurant along the transfer route
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration. The resort concierge will coordinate the exact departure transfer time based on your outbound flight details. Confirm all luggage is packed the night before. Costa Rica requires no departure tax for international flights as it is typically included in ticket prices — verify with your airline.
